A four-day week can work well for small teams if output stays steady and coverage is handled.  
The strongest evidence comes from self-selected trials that already had low turnover and good processes.  
Where people disagree is whether the gains are real or just a result of those pre-existing conditions.

**Self-selection bias**: Most trials are run by firms already doing well, so results may not generalize.  
**Coverage gaps**: Customer-facing teams often struggle to maintain service levels without extra staff or rotating schedules.  
**Work redesign vs. compression**: Gains only appear when work is redesigned, not when 40 hours are simply squeezed into 4 days.  
**Trial duration**: Critics note that most studies are short-term, leaving long-term sustainability unproven.
